rationale: A view may or may not be routable (modals, drawers); the boolean is correct. Only the old one-line description ('Routable grouping') was loose, and the proposed definition ('either the target of a navigation route or opened as a standalone surface') already says so.

Verified: accesscondition.source is a required string with no description, while nine security siblings declare source as an optional 'Source code reference' object. Same name, different meaning and type. This exact collision class caused the 0.1.11 attribute-drop bug (41 schemas). Fix is a rename or retype, so breaking.

Verified both files exist: accesscondition composes policyrule and policyrule uses accesscondition. Everywhere else composes runs whole -> part (navigationflow composes flowstep, userworkflow composes workflowstep); a rule composes conditions, not the reverse. Modellers following CLI suggestions will record it backwards.

False claim: there is exactly one applicationcomponent uses applicationcomponent schema. The proposer saw it twice because the prompt listed outgoing and incoming relationships separately and a self-relationship is both. The relationship list in the triage context shows it once.

Verified: protocol enum has HTTP and HTTPS while the attribute's own description says transport-level concerns such as TLS belong in the Technology layer. Merging values removes an enum value, so existing models using HTTPS need migration.
Verified: eight of nine application types declare a 'properties' object; applicationinteraction does not. Additive fix.

The proposed dataobject definition distinguishes only in-layer siblings (component, event, interface) and says nothing about data-model.objectschema or data-store entities, which is the confusion that matters for classification (Phase 0: application -> data-model was the top cross-layer confusion on dr-cli). A precedence rule in wording closes it.

DR deliberately uses its own predicate catalog (72 predicates with an archimate_alignment field) rather than ArchiMate relationship names; depends-on is aligned to ArchiMate Serving/Association by design.

Verified: namespace's description lists 'Elasticsearch index' as a namespace mapping while collection.collectionType has SEARCH_INDEX. One concept, two homes. Fix is wording: remove it from namespace (an Elasticsearch index holds documents; it is a collection).

The arrow direction is forced by the spec's rule that higher layers reference lower ones (api is layer 7, application layer 5), so 'inverted' is not a defect. Whether 'realizes' is the right predicate (versus serves/exposes, since an operation is an interface-level thing) is a modelling decision.
